latest_release.name: v2.3.1
latest_release.body:
DeepCode v2.3.1 is a stability release for the terminal UI on the shared background service. Answers now appear once and render as Markdown while they stream, the TUI survives a slow or restarted service, `/compact` works on coding sessions, and the background service no longer stops right after starting on Windows installs in a virtual environment. It also includes five community fixes and dependency security updates.

## Highlights

- **Answers shown once, rendered as Markdown.** The TUI no longer prints an answer a second time when it finishes, and a stopped answer keeps the text already shown. Headings, lists, bold text and tables are formatted as each line completes; code blocks are not indented or wrapped by DeepCode, so they copy back exactly; links show their address; and the line still being written is previewed above the status line. `/raw` prints answers exactly as written. The reasoning card comes before the answer, `Ctrl+O` mid-answer no longer repeats or drops lines, and text such as `root:x:0` or `:smile:` is no longer turned into emoji. See [The terminal UI](https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/blob/v2.3.1/docs/guide/the-tui.md).
- **A TUI that keeps working.** A failed request, an unrenderable event, or a restarted service no longer closes the TUI; `/reconnect` starts the service again when needed. Typing, completion, `Enter` and `Ctrl+C` stay responsive while the service is busy, and a slow answer is reported instead of retried three times. `Esc` interrupts only from an empty prompt and `Ctrl+C` first clears your draft, so a message you are typing is never lost or sent by accident.
- **Settings that stay current.** Default model and access changes show up in the TUI, `/new` follows your defaults, an approval answered in another client is announced, and `/goal clear out …` sets a new objective instead of clearing the Goal.
- **`/compact` that works on coding sessions.** Compaction runs in its Session's turn, so a message sent meanwhile waits for the summary and the next reply does not start with a failed request. Tool-call arguments, such as the file a `write_file` call carries, now count, so a session that wrote large files compacts instead of being refused as "would not shrink". A refusal says why. (#258)
- **The Windows service stays up.** On a Windows install in a virtual environment, the background service stopped right after it reported ready, whichever of the TUI, `deepcode service start`, or `deepcode web` launched it. It now stays up.
- **Community fixes.** Diff lines that contain a Unicode line separator or a form feed stay whole (#253); web fetch refuses private addresses tunnelled through NAT64 or IPv4-compatible IPv6 (#254); the destructive-command screen also catches absolute paths such as `/bin/rm -rf /` (#255); and `glob` finds files when the project sits under a directory named `build` or `venv` (#256).
- **Security updates.** pypdf, PyJWT, urllib3, and multidict move to patched releases.

## Upgrading

`pip install -U deepcode-hku`, then `deepcode service restart` so the background service runs the new version. The TUI tells you when the client and the service versions differ.

## Thanks

This release includes contributions from @KennyMcSimpson, @raymondginger2018-sudo, @D41910, and @liuzhengyang699, and @raymondginger2018-sudo and @rifkir23 tracked down the cause of the failing Windows CI job. Thank you.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/compare/v2.3.0...v2.3.1

DeepCode v2.3.1 是一次针对共享后台服务下终端界面的稳定性更新：回答只显示一次，并且边输出边渲染成 Markdown；后台服务变慢或重启时 TUI 照常工作；`/compact` 能压缩写代码的会话；在 Windows 上把 DeepCode 装在虚拟环境里时，后台服务不再刚启动就退出。本版本还包含五项社区修复和依赖的安全更新。

## 亮点

- **回答只显示一次，并渲染成 Markdown。** 回答结束时，TUI 不再把整段重新打印一遍；被中断的回答会保留已经输出的文字。标题、列表、粗体和表格在每行写完时排好；代码块不缩进，DeepCode 也不会给它折行，复制出来和原文一致；链接显示完整地址；还没写完的那一行先在状态行上方预览。`/raw` 按原文输出。推理卡片显示在回答之前；回答途中按 `Ctrl+O` 不会再重复或丢行；`root:x:0`、`:smile:` 这类文字不再被替换成表情。参见[终端界面指南](https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/blob/v2.3.1/docs/guide/the-tui.md)（英文）。
- **TUI 不再轻易中断。**

# DeepCode: Open Agentic Coding ### *Advancing Code Generation with Multi-Agent Systems*

### 🖥️ **Interface Showcase** #### 🖥️ **DeepCode Desktop**
*Work with DeepCode in a visual workspace for Sessions, goals, tool activity, code changes, and verification.*
DeepCode provides TUI, Desktop, and Web clients over one shared local service. They share Projects, Session history, models, Skills, permissions, Goals, and Automations. Use `deepcode`, `deepcode desktop`, or `deepcode web`; see [Quick start](#quick-start) for installation and your first task. ---
### 🎬 **Introduction Video**
*🎯 **Watch the DeepCode V2 introduction** - Long-horizon tasks, loop engineering, the agent harness, and self-evolution in 100 seconds*

--- > *"Where AI Agents Transform Ideas into Production-Ready Code"*
--- ## 📑 Table of Contents - [📰 What's new](#whats-new) - [🧠 What Deep means in DeepCode](#what-deep-means-in-deepcode) - [💡 Why DeepCode](#why-deepcode) - [⚡ Quick start](#quick-start) - [🖥️ Choosing a client](#choosing-a-client) - [📋 Requirements and platforms](#requirements-and-platforms) - [🚀 Core features](#core-features) - [🔒 Security and data](#security-and-data) - [📚 Documentation](#documentation) - [🔬 Research origin](#research-origin) - [🎬 Live Demonstrations](#live-demonstrations) - [🤝 Contributing](#contributing) - [💬 Support](#support) - [⭐ Star History](#star-history) - [🙏 Appreciation](#contributors) - [📖 Citation](#citation) - [📄 License](#license)

--- ## What's new - **2026-11-02** — Goals you can trust to finish: the agent proposes a checklist, and once you confirm it DeepCode runs those commands itself before it accepts "complete"; an optional independent reviewer checks every requirement, switched on in Settings, and each check is shown on the Goal card. A Goal can have a time limit, stops when it is stuck or keeps repeating itself, wraps up when its budget runs out, and pauses when DeepCode restarts. - **2026-10-31** — Long tasks read better on the Web (folded steps, a Goal outcome, faster long Sessions), declined tools say so, the terminal UI wraps Chinese text and resumes a running Turn cleanly, the Chinese interface has no stray English, the sidebar becomes a drawer on a narrow window, and the Web and Desktop interface is calmer: one typeface, one-line controls and steps, and fewer boxes and labels. - **2026-10-29** — Optional microcompact that clears old tool output before summarizing (`agents.defaults.microcompact`), an optional check before a Goal completes (`goal.completionVerifier`), folder browsing in the Web client, an opt-in risk check (`DEEPCODE_RISK_EVALUATOR=1`), and approval for project hooks (`deepcode hooks status` / `approve`). Clearer approvals: the TUI shows when it waits for you and what will change, "always allow" covers one kind of command instead of the whole tool, and trusting a folder asks first.
Earlier updates - **2026-10-28** — Agent presets that remove tools, file tools that ask before writing hooks, and unpinned MCP packages flagged - **2026-10-21** — A quiet Windows service, a separate code font, and community fixes - **2026-10-14** — Sessions that keep their history, a tighter sandbox, and the Desktop and Web apps in Chinese - **2026-10-13** — Smoother streaming, a self-managing background service, and safer Web sign-in - **2026-10-12** — DeepCode v2.3.1: Markdown answers in the TUI, a Windows service that stays up, `/compact` for coding sessions, and community fixes - **2026-10-10** — A steadier terminal UI: answers shown once, keys that keep your draft, and an orderly `/compact` - **2026-09-28** — DeepCode v2.3.0: voice dictation, Opper and Bedrock, Desktop polish, and opt-in hardening - **2026-09-09** — TUI, Desktop, and Web share one local background service - **2026-09-06** — DeepCode v2.2.0: Session context-window caps, compaction that leaves a memory, and a fully localized Desktop - **2026-09-03** — Desktop catalog race, an honest command screen, GLM-5.2, and two dependency bumps - **2026-08-28** — Community fixes: plugin credential warnings and a wider zh-CN Desktop - **2026-08-25** — Command executors close two bypasses - **2026-08-23** — Five repaired contributions land together - **2026-08-19** — Sessions that survive resume, compaction, and a second window - **2026-08-18** — Steadier context handling in the runtime, and the TUI gets a face - **2026-08-17** — Fixes from a review pass over the new settings and TUI work - **2026-08-16** — The TUI answers every bare command with a selector - **2026-08-15** — Settings grow up: a new settings dialog, declared models, and a safer config - **2026-08-14** — Subagent runtime, compaction, and one-way persistence - **2026-08-13** — Desktop typography, themes, and native controls - **2026-08-12** — Reviewed upstream core Skills, a managed MCP catalog, OAuth, and real connection checks - **2026-08-10** — Generic MCP runtime and portable local Plugins - **2026-08-09** — Skills now have a real runtime contract - **2026-08-07** — Thinking controls, more providers, and a Desktop you can tune - **2026-08-04** — Skills that work wherever you do - **2026-08-03** — 🎉 DeepCode v2.0 is here - **2026-07-31** — One execution model across CLI and Desktop - **2026-07-21** — Durable Goals and safe Session lifecycle - **2026-07-20** — Session-level model control and shared Skills - **2026-07-17** — Durable Session navigation and replay - **2026-07-10** — Loop Engineering and parallel agents - **2026-07-08** — General coding agent, durable Sessions, and memory - **2026-07-04** — Agent Harness foundation - Earlier history: [legacy README](docs/archive/README_LEGACY_2026-07-20.md)
All changes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). --- ## What Deep means in DeepCode Most Coding Agents can generate code. The hard part is understanding a real project, making changes within the right boundaries, continuously correcting course from runtime results, and making it clear why the outcome can be trusted. DeepCode is an open-source Coding Agent for real software engineering. Give it a simple change or a goal that takes dozens of steps. It can understand the project, work on the code, run tools, verify results, and continue after an interruption, restart, or model switch. “Deep” represents four kinds of depth that remain with the task from start to finish: | Depth | What it means for you | | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Deep Context** | Understand the task through project structure, engineering rules, Skills, Session history, and long-term memory. | | **Deep Execution** | Search, edit, run commands, and execute tests instead of stopping at suggestions—and show the work as it happens. | | **Deep Verification** | Check results with tests, builds, diagnostics, Diffs, and task Artifacts rather than treating a plausible answer as done. | | **Deep Continuity** | Preserve conversations, decisions, tool records, and evidence across time, directories, clients, and model changes. | DeepCode stands out in three ways: - **Done means checked.** When the agent says a Goal is complete, DeepCode runs the checklist you confirmed itself, and an optional independent reviewer proves each requirement with evidence. A claim that falls short goes back to the agent with what is missing. - **Keep long tasks moving while staying in control.** A Goal is not a one-shot prompt. Add requirements, revise the Goal, pause, stop, or continue while the task is running without losing completed work. It also stops on its own when it is stuck, out of budget or out of time. - **Every change can be reviewed.** Edits show as diffs, sensitive actions wait for your approval, and each Goal keeps its tool calls and checks, so you can see why the outcome can be trusted. DeepCode is not designed to make an Agent look busier. It is designed to help you finish real software engineering work more reliably. --- ## Why DeepCode - **Work that outlasts one answer.** Give the agent a Goal and it keeps working across turns, checking its results, until it reports the Goal complete or blocked, and a completion claim is checked before it counts. You can add requirements, edit the Goal, pause or stop it while it runs. - **Keeps running when you close the client.** Turns run in a local background service, not in the window you started them from. Close the TUI, reopen the session in the browser, and answer the pending approval there. - **One session, four clients.** The TUI, Desktop, Web and `deepcode exec` read and write the same projects, sessions, models, Skills and permissions. - **You decide what it may do.** A folder must be trusted before the agent works in it. Each session runs under Ask, Read only or Full access, shell commands run in an OS sandbox under Ask, and repository hooks need your approval. Use any of 14 built-in providers, your own OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, or a local model.

The Web client after a real Goal: the agent fixed two bugs and added tests, DeepCode ran the confirmed checks, and an independent review proved every requirement before the Goal counted as complete.

## Quick start **1. Install.** With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): ```console uv tool install --python 3.12 deepcode-hku deepcode init ``` `deepcode init` creates `~/.deepcode` and sets the default access to **Ask**. If your shell cannot find `deepcode`, run `uv tool update-shell` and open a new terminal. On Windows, install uv with `winget install --id astral-sh.uv --exact`. **2. Add a model.** This example uses OpenRouter; any [supported provider](#models-and-providers) works the same way. The key is read without echo and stored in `~/.deepcode/credentials.json`. ```console deepcode provider set my-openrouter --template openrouter --api-key deepcode provider models my-openrouter --refresh deepcode provider test my-openrouter --model MODEL_ID ``` Replace `MODEL_ID` with a model from the list. In Desktop or Web you can do the same under **Settings → Models**.
**3. Run it in a project.** ```console cd /path/to/your-project deepcode --trust --connection my-openrouter --model MODEL_ID ``` `--trust` is needed once per project. Later, run `deepcode` in that folder and use `/model` to switch models. Try a first task: ```text Explain how this project is organized and how to run its tests. Do not change any files yet. ``` The step-by-step tutorial is [Your first coding task](docs/guide/getting-started.md). ## Choosing a client All clients connect to the same local service, so a session started in one can be continued in any other. | Client | Start with | Use it for | |---|---|---| | **TUI** | `deepcode` | Working in the terminal. See [The terminal UI](docs/guide/the-tui.md). | | **Web** | `deepcode web` | The full workbench (diffs, files, terminal, Goals) in your browser, from the same install. See [Web client](docs/WEB_CLIENT.md). | | **Desktop** | `deepcode desktop` | The same workbench as a native app. Runs from a source checkout for now, see [below](#desktop). | | **Headless** | `deepcode exec ""` | One turn from a script or CI job; `--json` prints events as NDJSON. `deepcode loop ""` runs a Goal. See [Headless and automation](docs/HEADLESS_AND_AUTOMATION.md). | `deepcode web --no-open` prints the sign-in link instead of opening a browser. The link works once and expires after 60 seconds. ### Desktop There are no Desktop installers on the Releases page yet. Desktop runs from a source checkout and needs Node.js 22+, Rust (stable) and the [Tauri 2 prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) for your platform: ```console git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode.git cd DeepCode npm --prefix desktop ci npm --prefix desktop run build:web uv tool install --python 3.12 --force . deepcode init deepcode desktop ``` The first launch builds the app's resources and takes a few minutes; keep the terminal open while Desktop runs. Windows toolchains and troubleshooting are in the [Desktop guide](desktop/README.md). ### The background service Starting any client starts the service if it is not running. Closing a client leaves accepted work running; pending approvals wait for you, and the computer must stay awake. | Task | Command | |---|---| | Check whether it is running | `deepcode service status` | | Read recent logs | `deepcode service logs --lines 100` | | Stop after current work finishes | `deepcode service stop --drain --timeout 60` | | Start it when you log in | `deepcode service install --at-login` | Upgrades and backups: [Upgrading DeepCode](docs/UPGRADE_AND_RESTORE.md). Problems: [Troubleshooting](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md). ## Requirements and platforms | | | |---|---| | Python | 3.12 or later (CI tests 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14) | | Operating systems | macOS, Linux and Windows | | Tools | Git, for change review and worktrees. On Linux, bubblewrap (`bwrap`) for the command sandbox. | | Model | An API key for a supported provider, or a local Ollama or vLLM server. The model must support tool calling; `deepcode provider test --agent` checks it. | | Web client | A current browser on the same computer | | Desktop | Node.js 22+, Rust and the Tauri prerequisites (source build) | ## Core features

- **Repository work.** Reads, searches and edits files, applies patches, runs commands and tests, and shows each change as a diff. [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md) - **Goals.** `/goal ` in the TUI or the Goal panel in Desktop and Web. The Goal continues across turns and is kept across restarts. Its completion is checked: DeepCode runs the checklist you confirmed, and an independent reviewer can prove each requirement (Settings → General). A token budget or time limit bounds it. [Goals and automation](docs/guide/goals-and-headless.md) - **Sessions and context.** Every session is saved with its tool calls, approvals and Goal state. `/resume`, `/compact` and per-session context caps keep long work going. [Sessions](docs/guide/sessions.md) - **Project instructions and memory.** Reads `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and keeps project notes in `.deepcode/memory/`. [Skills and memory](docs/guide/skills-and-memory.md) - **Models and providers.** Named connections, per-session model and reasoning effort, and connection checks before use. [Models and providers](docs/guide/models.md) - **Skills and plugins.** Reusable instructions from `.agents/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, eight bundled Skills, and a Skill creator. Plugins package Skills and MCP servers. [Skills](docs/guide/skills-and-memory.md) · [Local plugins](docs/LOCAL_PLUGINS.md) - **MCP.** Connects to stdio, SSE and Streamable HTTP servers, with a bundled catalog and OAuth sign-in. `deepcode mcp serve` exposes DeepCode itself as an MCP server. [MCP guide](docs/integrations/MCP.md) - **Agent presets and sub-agents.** Presets set a persona and narrow the tool set. Sub-agents can work in separate Git worktrees. [Configuration](docs/guide/configuration.md#agent-presets) - **Automations.** Run a saved instruction on a schedule with the same agent, permissions and history. [Automations](docs/guide/goals-and-headless.md#persistent-interval-automations) - **Voice input.** Optional dictation in the Desktop and Web composer. [Voice dictation](docs/guide/dictation.md) - **Paper2Code.** Turn a paper or technical document into a code base. [Paper2Code](docs/paper2code.md) ### Models and providers Built-in templates: OpenRouter, Requesty, Opper, Forge, Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, Zhipu AI, DashScope, MiniMax, Ollama and vLLM. A **Custom** connection points at any endpoint that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages API. `deepcode provider list` shows them and which ones are ready. ## Security and data - **Data stays on your computer.** Settings, sessions, state and logs are under `~/.deepcode` (or `$DEEPCODE_HOME`). Project notes are in `/.deepcode/memory/`. DeepCode has no account system and sends no analytics. - **Local service.** The background service listens on `127.0.0.1` only (port 3081, or a free port if that is taken). Native clients authenticate with a private token; the Web client signs in with a one-time link. - **Project trust.** The agent does not run in a folder you have not trusted. A project's own config cannot select Full access, turn off the sandbox or redirect model requests. - **Access presets and approvals.** **Ask** asks before edits and commands and runs shell commands in an OS sandbox; **Read only** denies changes; **Full access** removes approvals and the sandbox. Your `deny` rules apply under every preset. - **Hooks.** Hooks a repository declares run only after you approve them; changed hooks wait for `deepcode hooks approve`. - **Credentials.** API keys are stored in `~/.deepcode/credentials.json` with owner-only permissions and never returned to a client. Shell commands do not see them. - **What model providers receive.** The system prompt, project instructions, tool definitions, the conversation and tool results (file contents, command output) go to the endpoint of the connection you chose. `providers.egress` can restrict which hosts are allowed. A local model keeps everything on your machine. Details: [Security and data](docs/guide/security.md). To report a vulnerability, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | Topic | Guide | |---|---| | First task, step by step | [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md) | | Terminal UI keys and commands | [The terminal UI](docs/guide/the-tui.md) | | Resume, compact and manage sessions | [Sessions](docs/guide/sessions.md) | | Providers, local models, reasoning | [Models and providers](docs/guide/models.md) | | Project instructions, memory, Skills | [Skills and memory](docs/guide/skills-and-memory.md) | | Goals, automations, headless runs | [Goals and automation](docs/guide/goals-and-headless.md) | | Config file and environment variables | [Configuration](docs/guide/configuration.md) | | Data, sandbox, approvals | [Security and data](docs/guide/security.md) | | Startup and connection problems | [Troubleshooting](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md) | | Scripts, CI and administration | [Headless and automation](docs/HEADLESS_AND_AUTOMATION.md) | | MCP servers | [MCP guide](docs/integrations/MCP.md) | | Background service | [Local background service](docs/SERVICE_RUNTIME.md) | | Upgrades and backups | [Upgrading DeepCode](docs/UPGRADE_AND_RESTORE.md) | | Desktop from source | [Desktop guide](desktop/README.md) | | Paper2Code | [Paper2Code](docs/paper2code.md) | ## Research origin DeepCode started as Paper2Code, a multi-agent system that turns research papers into working code. On [PaperBench](https://openai.com/index/paperbench/) it scored 75.9% on the human-expert subset, above the best reported human baseline (72.4%). The method is described in [DeepCode: Open Agentic Coding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.07921). Paper2Code is still available in Desktop and Web; see [Paper2Code](docs/paper2code.md).

## 🎬 Live Demonstrations These recordings show projects produced by earlier DeepCode workflows. They are output demonstrations rather than screenshots of the current Desktop UI.
#### 📄 Paper2Code **Research to implementation** **[▶ Watch demonstration](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MQZYpLkzsbw)** Reproduce a research paper as an executable project. #### 🖼️ Generated vision project **Image workflow example** **[▶ Watch demonstration](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFt5mLaMEac)** See an earlier generated image-processing workflow in use. #### 🌐 Generated web project **Frontend implementation example** **[▶ Watch demonstration](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=78wx3dkTaAU)** Follow a complete frontend implementation from idea to result.
The [DeepCode V2 introduction video](https://youtu.be/TxwBHRQoaBw) gives a broader walkthrough. --- ## Contributing Development setup, checks and pull request guidelines are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Everyone who has opened a pull request is listed in [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). ## Support - Bugs and feature requests: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/issues) - Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) - Community: the Feishu and WeChat groups listed on the [HKUDS profile](https://github.com/HKUDS/.github/blob/main/profile/README.md) --- ## ⭐ Star History
